title: Tulsi Gabbard's Brother Charged With Trying to Lure Children at Waikiki Hotel
excerpt: Batarti Gabbard, 55, was arrested on custodial interference charges after allegedly offering children gum and money to accompany him to his hotel room. His family says he is in the grip of a mental health crisis.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Batarti Gabbard, 55, was charged with custodial interference for allegedly luring children at a hotel.
  • He offered children gum and money, writing their names in a notebook before they refused.
  • Family cites a severe mental health crisis following a decade of stability and erratic behavior.
  • Tulsi Gabbard has not commented on her brother's arrest amid personal family challenges.
Incident Overview
›Date of incident: July 12
›Location: Waikiki hotel pool
›Charges: Second-degree custodial interference
›Victims: Several children approached
›Reported by: A 42-year-old woman
  • Batarti Gabbard, 55, the older brother of former U.S. Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, has been charged with second-degree custodial interference after allegedly approaching children at a Waikiki hotel pool on July 12.
  • The Honolulu Police Department says Gabbard offered children gum and money to accompany him to his hotel room and wrote their names in a notebook. The children refused.
  • His father, Hawaii State Sen. Mike Gabbard, says Batarti is experiencing a severe mental health crisis after a decade of stability and is under psychiatric evaluation.
  • Tulsi Gabbard, who resigned as DNI in May after her husband's cancer diagnosis, has not publicly commented on the arrest.

Batarti Gabbard, the older brother of former U.S. Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, was arrested and charged on July 17 after he allegedly tried to lure children into his hotel room at a Waikiki resort, the Honolulu Police Department said.

Gabbard, 55, faces a charge of second-degree custodial interference in connection with what police described as a "stranger danger incident" on July 12 at the pool area of an unnamed Waikiki hotel.

"At about 2:00 p.m., an unknown man allegedly approached several children, including a 9-year-old boy, and offered them gum and money to accompany him to his hotel room."

— Honolulu Police Department statement

Police said Gabbard also asked the children for their names, which he wrote in a notebook. The children refused and he walked away. A 42-year-old woman subsequently reported the incident to authorities, according to KITV. No children were physically harmed.

Family Points to Mental Health Crisis

Batarti — who also goes by his given Hindu name, Bhakti — is the eldest son of Hawaii State Sen. Mike Gabbard, 78. In a statement to the Honolulu Star-Advertiser, the senator and his wife Carol said their son had been stable for the past decade before a sudden deterioration.

"Bhakti has had mental issues in the past but has been doing well for the last 10 years. His wife kicked him out of the house, so he's been sleeping on the streets. He gave away his car to a homeless person; lost his ID and phone and has no money."

— Sen. Mike Gabbard and Carol Gabbard, statement to Honolulu Star-Advertiser

According to the family, Batarti began behaving erratically after smoking marijuana, renaming himself "Batarti" and claiming to be "Jim Morrison Jr." His wife, Kimberly Gabbard, filed a protective order against him on July 11 — the day before the hotel incident — citing "erratic, impulsive and bizarre behavior," according to the Honolulu Star-Advertiser. She told the court he had previously been diagnosed with bipolar disorder.

Mental Health Crisis
›Batarti's mental health deteriorated after a decade of stability.
›Previous diagnosis: Bipolar disorder.
›Recent erratic behavior linked to marijuana use.
›Placed on a 72-hour psychiatric hold.

Batarti was taken to Queen's Hospital for a psychological evaluation, where he reportedly told doctors they would find "cocaine, ice and pot in his blood tests," according to People magazine. He was placed on a 72-hour psychiatric hold. In a separate statement to Fox News, Sen. Gabbard confirmed his son continues to receive treatment. "We love him, and asked him to follow the protocol at the hospital, which he says he will do," he said.

Separate Theft Charge and Custody Status

Gabbard was separately arrested on July 16 for theft, to which he pleaded not guilty the following day, according to KITV. He is scheduled to return to court for that charge on August 14. No court date has been set for the custodial interference case. He remains in police custody.

Tulsi Gabbard's Silence

Tulsi Gabbard has not publicly commented on her brother's arrest. The 45-year-old former congresswoman resigned as Trump's DNI on May 22 after her husband, Abraham Williams, was diagnosed with an extremely rare form of bone cancer. She had overseen the coordination of 18 U.S. intelligence agencies since February 2025. Bill Pulte has been serving as acting DNI since June 19.

Diaspora Significance

Legal Status
›Arrested on July 16 for theft.
›Plea: Not guilty.
›Next court date for theft: August 14.
›Custodial interference case: No court date set.

The case adds a personal dimension to a figure of particular significance to the Indian-American diaspora. Tulsi Gabbard, who is of Samoan heritage and was raised in a Hindu household in Hawaii, became the first Hindu elected to the U.S. Congress in 2012, taking her oath of office on the Bhagavad Gita. The Gabbard family's Hindu roots — Batarti's given name, Bhakti, means "devotion" in Sanskrit — have been a recurring element of public interest.

Batarti Gabbard remains in custody and is receiving psychiatric care. The Honolulu Police Department has said its investigation into the hotel pool incident is ongoing.
